summary: Memory-floor case: amdclang's build already runs at reference headroom 0.96 to 1.07 (337.8 MB read + 335.5 MB written in ~0.123 ms; every element touched exactly once, no re-reads), so 1.5x is out of reach and was not reached. The shipped state 94d64e2d773e1168 is a source rewrite: loop-free threads that each rotate 4 pairs with 16-byte global_load/store_dwordx4 (x, y, cos, sin), one flat head index over query then key, one 640-thread workgroup per token (grid N x cdiv((Hq+Hk)*16, 640)); generic strided loop and scalar tail keep it correct for other shapes. It passes the full battery (98/98) and measured 1.053x (CI 1.0505-1.0557) and 1.043x (CI 1.0411-1.0465) in two 240-pair timings (1.036x at 60 pairs). Results meet the manifest tolerance, not bit-identity (v_pk_fma contraction).

friction: coarsen refused on source state 94d64e2d773e1168: 'coarsen: `s_add_u32 s24, s0, 0x60`: the kernarg pointer is used other than as the base of a scalar load'. amdclang forms kernarg+0x60 to read the hidden dispatch arguments (gridDim/blockDim at 0x60+4 and 0x6c); coarsen should accept a kernarg-derived base (or source should offer a way to pass grid/block sizes as launch args without the hidden-arg block).

The number of tokens N is not a kernel parameter, so more than one token per workgroup needed an appended launch arg; fine, but a hint in info() that shape symbols can be appended as args would save a step.

Two timings were flagged 'disturbed' (38b35c3c518222bc, cfbd1bb5f81342fb) and one of them reported a 'win' at 1.064 that was 0.995 at 240 pairs: a disturbed run should probably not carry an outcome of win/loss at all, or bench should retry automatically.

reference_ms moved between 0.1214 and 0.1349 ms across benches (clock levels 983 to 2400 MHz), so headroom of the same reference read 0.96 to 1.07; a headroom computed from the best-clock run would be steadier.

No way to express a non-uniform block (640 threads with waves that mix query and key heads is fine, but a launch whose block equals (Hq+Hk)*16 needed a hard-coded 640 with BLK define; block expressions over shape symbols work, I used a define only for the sweep).
lessons: vl_rotary_embedding (in-place RoPE over 335 MB, each element read and written once) is at the memory floor in amdclang's build: 0.123 ms against a floor model of 0.126 ms (headroom 0.96-1.07). Best achievable was 1.04-1.05x; no bytes can be saved because cos/sin (512 B per token) are negligible.

At the floor, workgroup size mattered more than anything else for the loop-free 16B-per-lane form: per token (640 threads of work) block 64 -> 0.853x, block 256 -> 0.999x, block 320 -> ~0.96x (noisy), block 640 (exactly one workgroup per token, 16384 workgroups of 10 waves) -> 1.043-1.053x. This differs from fi_silu_and_mul where block 64/256/1024 were within 2%: here 164K one-wave workgroups cost 15%.

32 bytes per lane (two dwordx4 groups per thread for each of x and y) lost again on a kernel that already moves 16 bytes per lane: 0.837x (1 token per workgroup), 0.765x (2 tokens per workgroup). Confirms the fi_silu_and_mul / copy-study note.

Two tokens per workgroup via a per-thread loop over tokens (half the workgroups, same waves): 0.995x at 240 pairs, i.e. nothing over one token per workgroup; the gain from 4 bytes to 16 bytes per lane plus loop-free threads is the whole 4-5%.
A 60-pair bench flagged 'disturbed' gave 1.064 for a state that is 0.995 at 240 pairs: always re-time disturbed runs before building on them.

amdclang turns a float4 (ext_vector_type(4), aligned(4)) rotation into global_load_dwordx4 x4 + v_pk_mul/v_pk_fma with all four loads in flight and staged vmcnt(2)/(1)/(0) waits by itself; an unsigned divide by a runtime value costs ~15 VALU instructions per wave (reciprocal hoisted), which is invisible at the memory floor.

session.final:
The 1.5x target was not reached: the best verified state is `94d64e2d773e1168` at about 1.04x over amdclang, and the report is filed with it as the state to ship.

**Why 1.5x is out of reach:** this is the memory-floor case. amdclang's build already runs at headroom 0.96 to 1.07, reading 338 MB and writing 336 MB with every element touched exactly once. There are no re-reads to remove, so no bytes can be saved.

**What the winning state does:** it is a source rewrite. Each thread rotates 4 pairs with 16-byte loads and stores and no loop, using one flat head index over query then key and one 640-thread workgroup per token. It passes the full battery (98/98) and two 240-pair timings gave 1.053x (CI 1.0505–1.0557) and 1.043x (CI 1.0411–1.0465). Results meet the manifest tolerance but are not bit-identical to the baseline.

**What else was tried** (same loop-free form unless noted):

| Variant | Speedup | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Block 64 (10 one-wave workgroups per token) | 0.853 | loss |
| Block 256 | 0.999 | parity |
| Block 320 | 0.96 | loss (disturbed run) |
| Block 640, two tokens per workgroup | 0.995 | parity at 240 pairs |
| 32 bytes per lane, one token per workgroup | 0.837 | loss |
| 32 bytes per lane, two tokens per workgroup | 0.765 | loss |
| `coarsen` on the best state | — | refused |

- **Disturbed timing:** the two-tokens variant first showed 1.064x in a disturbed 60-pair run; the 240-pair re-time put it at parity.
- **`coarsen` refusal:** it rejects the state because amdclang forms `kernarg + 0x60` to read the grid and block sizes. This is logged as friction.
- **Machine level:** I made no machine-level edits. The hot path is already straight-line with four wide loads in flight and late waits, so I judged nothing there could differ measurably at this headroom.
